about: Claims from Bounty's YouTube commentary (October 2026 monthly playoffs), paraphrased (never the transcript: public repo). Each claim: approximate match time in seconds (set from the anchor named; the transcripts have no timestamps), kind (plan, read, call, reason, prediction, diagnosis, technique), the claim, tactics ids, the variable it suggests (comms_vars.py), and the engine's check: agrees, disagrees, partly, or can't measure, with the evidence. Bounty plays mesmer for 옷옷옷옷, so weigh his comments on their games with that in mind. Vocabulary: footies = footmen; Ellie = elementalist; cycle = a 2-minute window in which a team can push, do damage and deal with the split; inaccuracies = small errors that add up (Bounty's chess comparison).

3dd84ec7-29f5-578d-a7ad-42a272bff049.map: Isle of Meditation (Bounty called it Volcano)
3dd84ec7-29f5-578d-a7ad-42a272bff049.result: Crew won at about 20:29 by killing BcS's Lord in a base race
3dd84ec7-29f5-578d-a7ad-42a272bff049.alignment: Crew Monk 1 (Ray of Judgment smite splitter) death 0:52, BcS archer and two knights 2:39, BcS overcapped 8:14 -> 8:17, BcS Mesmer flag death 12:05, Crew Mesmer death at the stand 15:41, BcS wipe in Crew's base 16:39 to 17:16, BcS boost 17:33, Crew wipe 18:36 to 19:16

claims.claim: Crew's build sends a lone Ray of Judgment smite monk to split, babysat by the 8 or a ritualist; it kills NPCs well but does almost nothing against players.

check.evidence: Crew's Monk 1 split from 0:35 and alone 3:05 to 3:53; BcS lost an archer (0:58), then an archer and two knights at 2:39 with no Crew death there.

claims.claim: BcS's snares suit this matchup: the smite splitter stays snared after teleporting back, so he can still be collapsed and struggles to reach the pit.

check.evidence: Crew's Monk 1 died twice (0:52 backside, 5:01 push side) but still reached the pit at 2:39 and 12:53 (bodyguard). Across 144 matches, collapses with a snare carrier among the defenders (Return not counted) killed a splitter 20% of the time against 11% without (supported, +6.5 points, interval +1 to +13).

claims.claim: The smite monk's early Shadow Step put him in trouble at the back footmen.

check.evidence: Crew Monk 1 died at 0:52 on the backside (4v6).

claims.claim: BcS's paragon kited away from his team and died for it.

check.evidence: BcS Paragon died at 2:58 on the backside.

claims.claim: BcS is never a unit: with two Fall Backs and a God Speed it should move together, but it is always scattered, so when it fills gaps on the map it isn't all there to kill.

check.evidence: Denning: Bounty is speaking metaphorically here, so the claim isn't tested.

claims.claim: Capping a flag that gets overcapped at once wastes a cycle; if you will be overcapped instantly, don't cap.

check.evidence: BcS capped at 8:14 and Crew overcapped at 8:17 (3 s). Across 144 matches 16% of captures are overcapped within 10 s; those runs took longer (45 s against 37 s), and from the start of the run to 30 s after the capture the capturing team lost more players than it killed 22% of the time against 16% (supported, +8.6 points, interval +3 to +16). Partly the situation: an instant overcap means the enemy was ready at the stand.

claims.claim: By 14:00 BcS had wasted its cycles: Crew had almost no death penalty, BcS had killed one knight, and BcS's own pit was empty with its Lord damaged.

check.evidence: Crew had 3 deaths by 14:00 (Monk 1 twice, Necromancer); BcS killed one Crew knight (13:22) and had lost four archers, two knights and the Bodyguard (0:58 to 12:53).

claims.claim: Capping invited Crew to stay and fight, and BcS killed the flag carrier: when you kill, the mistake doesn't matter.

check.evidence: BcS capped at 15:33; Crew's Mesmer died at the stand at 15:41.

claims.claim: Crew's rule: if a team pushes your pit with one monk, you kill it. BcS pushed with one monk at home and its main died very fast.

check.evidence: BcS lost 5 in Crew's base and the push side from 16:39 to 17:16 (wipe 5v6).

claims.claim: With Crew's third monk back, BcS's six-damage, one-monk push had to keep killing; it nearly finished, but Crew's Warrior resurrected the Flash mesmer, who resurrected the rest, and Crew found the open Lord to end it.

check.evidence: BcS killed four Crew players 18:36 to 19:16 and the Bodyguard at 19:49; Crew won the base race at about 20:29. Which resurrections happened isn't checked here.

f34cb3a9-98c7-53d0-a980-60aa7dd5bc8d.result: One won a flawless victory at about 15:35
f34cb3a9-98c7-53d0-a980-60aa7dd5bc8d.alignment: True's Dervish split from 0:34 (One archer 0:58), True deaths 0:56 to 1:43, One boosts 2:39, 4:39, 6:39, 10:32, 12:32, One knight lost at 14:10, True wipe 14:50 to 15:35

claims.claim: True ran its main team into the enemy short-handed (6v8, 7v8) while its Dervish capped and split; it didn't know the game state and was wiped early.

check.evidence: True's Dervish split from 0:34; True's first death came at 6v7 (0:56), then 7 Monk, Prot and Mes/A by 1:43.

claims.claim: One played very carefully after the early win, resetting rather than pushing its advantage.

check.evidence: Intent; One didn't kill again until 3:09.

claims.claim: When True had a 7v6 it needed to jump One; its damage didn't commit.

check.evidence: True held numbers advantages at 4:14 (7v5), 5:23 (8v7), 7:26 (5v4 for 60 s), 9:04, 9:58 (7v6, then 7v4) and 11:21, and killed no one in any of them.

claims.claim: One's Dervish dropped the flag to break a block that was about to fall anyway; with no backup flag, he should have kept it.

check.evidence: Blocks and drops aren't in the replay data.

claims.claim: One missed a boost by only about 7 or 8 seconds.

check.evidence: One boosted at 2:39, 4:39 and 6:39, then not at 8:39 (it recapped at 8:32), next at 10:32.

claims.claim: True's Dervish split into One's base and killed a knight, True's first accomplishment in 14 minutes, but his flag was overcapped so it didn't pay off.

check.evidence: One lost a knight at 14:10 to True's Dervish split; True had capped at 13:19 and One answered at 13:34.

claims.claim: A flawless victory: True never killed a single player, and kept missing the monks when it had chances.

check.evidence: No One deaths in the match; True wiped from 14:50.

9b0816e2-c0eb-5797-a1b1-9962c8415307.alignment: Apes wipe 0:41 to 1:34, Apes Necromancer split 2:13 to 3:56 and death 4:06, cope wipe 7:24 to 8:01, Apes Ritualist death 10:21, Apes wipes 11:06 to 11:59 and 15:52 to 17:10, cope boosts 2:57, 14:05, 16:05, 18:05

claims.claim: Apes' unusual build aims to get the flag game going: two Shadow of Haste characters, double run out front, push on the Balthazar dervish.

check.evidence: Apes capped at 0:41 with the Necromancer and split him from 2:13.

claims.claim: Apes' monks were hit hard in the opening and died within a minute; no build is good if you die in a minute.

check.evidence: Apes lost 6 players from 0:56 to 1:34 (wipe, first at 7v8).

claims.claim: Apes' Necromancer leaving the base alone was bound to cost his team, and he died after time.

check.evidence: Apes' Necromancer split 2:13 to 3:56 and died at 4:06 (within 15 s after 4:00, so after time).

claims.claim: cope respected the lone splitter more than it should have; winning the main fight, it could have ignored him and fought 8v7.

check.evidence: cope sent its Dervish, 8 Monk and Hammer (3:12); whether fighting 8v7 was better needs the usual-play comparison (step 4).

claims.claim: Apes had an 8v7 for about 90 seconds and didn't know it had to kill: its Dervish stayed far from anyone.

check.evidence: Apes did kill four cope players 7:24 to 8:01 (cope wiped), so the window wasn't wasted, though late.

claims.claim: Small errors added up (inaccuracies, not blunders): the 8 monk should have taken the flag sooner.

check.evidence: Who could take the flag when is a choice the replay doesn't record.

claims.claim: Apes' Ritualist got caught away from his team: a bad death, and Apes then spent its time fixing it (failed resurrections) and took more deaths.

check.evidence: Apes' Ritualist died at 10:21 (4v5, push side); Apes lost 5 more from 11:06 to 11:59.

claims.claim: Without the pressure from its base, Apes should solo split, wait for the answer, then push a flag; pushing 8v8 is a risk for this build.

check.evidence: Apes' 8v8 fights went badly: wipes at 11:27 and 15:52.

claims.claim: Never send both Shadow of Haste players (Necromancer and Ritualist) on a split; keep one in base.

check.evidence: Apes split Necromancer, Hammer, Ritualist and 8 Monk at 14:38 and lost that 4v4 (wipe 15:52); whether the split choice caused it isn't separated.

claims.claim: Apes should have won the 4v4 but lost it to layers of errors: a monk caught off his shield set by Coward, a sleepy 8, the Necromancer not watching the warrior.

check.evidence: Apes lost the 4v4 at 15:52 (Ritualist, 8 Monk, Hammer, Necromancer died 16:07 to 17:10); the shield-set and Coward detail can be read with forensics.py but isn't checked here.

49eec28d-0f4b-5cc1-a146-4d1ad0bd642b.result: OG won a base race: hold's Lord died at 5:17, OG's at 5:20
49eec28d-0f4b-5cc1-a146-4d1ad0bd642b.alignment: OG deaths 1:04 and 1:48, OG's four-player split 2:45, OG wipe 3:15 to 3:47, OG capture 3:47, both pits fall 3:48 to 5:20

claims.claim: Hex way is a hard matchup for triple melee; OG's mesmers had to do a very good job.

check.evidence: OG lost two players at main by 1:48 and turned to the split.

claims.claim: hold chose to fight at main early; it had built its monks (Divine Healing, double Blessed Light) to hold longer.

check.evidence: Choice of fight; the healing totals are in the match data.

claims.claim: Defending with two players says 'give us time to finish', so hold shouldn't have followed OG's split with axes; it wasted about 25 to 30 seconds, probably the biggest reason it lost.

check.evidence: The base race was decided by seconds (hold's Lord died at 5:17, OG's at 5:20; METHODS notes 0.3 s), so 25 to 30 s spent chasing is more than the margin.

claims.claim: OG's number 1 capping the flag wasted time in what became a base race, but that's only clear in hindsight.

check.evidence: OG capped at 3:47 during the race.

claims.claim: hold could instead have defended with both monks and pushed with the ritualist, since the ritualist only faced one mesmer.

check.evidence: A choice not taken; step 4 would price it.

claims.claim: hold was too hasty: it played offensively with two monks instead of defending more and working through the game.

check.evidence: A judgment over the whole match.

1d073205-fdec-5684-aa7a-b03a558a9471.alignment: hdm 4-4 split wiped 1:16 to 1:48, cope Ranger death 5:08, hdm deaths 7:36 to 8:14, hdm's six-player push takes cope's pit 15:21 to 15:58, cope's push wiped 19:25 to 21:31

claims.claim: hdm played a 4-4: two elementalists, a mesmer and a monk on the split, and the main team without its prot; very committed to the split.

check.evidence: hdm's split groups held both elementalists and a monk (e.g. 9:37).

claims.claim: hdm's first split group got bullied off the side, though cope didn't kill anyone after time.

check.evidence: hdm lost Air Ele, Fire Ele and Monk 4 at 1:31 to 1:48 on the push side (3v4), none within 15 s after a 2-minute mark.

claims.claim: cope's ranger should have stayed at the back door, to take free footmen and warn the team, since he leads the answer to splits.

check.evidence: Warnings aren't in the data.

claims.claim: cope's ranger death looked avoidable, but it cost no NPCs.

check.evidence: cope's Ranger died at 5:08 in its own pit; cope had lost an archer outside at 4:46, but nothing after the death.

claims.claim: hdm got killed again at main and was in trouble.

check.evidence: hdm lost Mes/A (7:36), Air Ele (7:48) and Monk 4 (8:14).

claims.claim: hdm then made its split beefier (ritualist and two elementalists); cope kept defending the same way and would lose for it.

check.evidence: hdm split Air Ele, Fire Ele, Ritualist and Dervish at 9:37; cope's pit fell later, at 15:30 to 15:58, to a six-player hdm push.

claims.claim: Answer the split with the prot; cope's main team gets no benefit from having it at main.

check.evidence: The usual-play comparison of defender choices needs step 4.

claims.claim: cope's main team did nothing for 19 minutes, killing one footman, then tried a push at the end and was wiped.

check.evidence: cope killed no hdm player after 8:14 until the end; its push at 19:25 lost 10 players by 21:31.

claims.claim: cope had guests (ranger and another) and without its core lineup looked lost.

check.evidence: Lineup strength is measured (lineup.py) but not checked against this claim here.

2df9b7fd-823e-5df7-ad4e-192612cd9249.teams: Team (double melee, ritualist, two mesmers) against push (monk spike: WoC monks with Return)
2df9b7fd-823e-5df7-ad4e-192612cd9249.alignment: Team 8 Monk death 1:50, push knight 2:10, push Snare death 4:16, push knight 4:29, Team boosts 5:44 and 14:16, push Bodyguard 8:52, push wipes 23:56 to 25:27

claims.claim: push collapsed Team's split, which is right on this map, but went for the 8 monk, not the best target.

check.evidence: Team's 8 Monk died at 1:50. Across 144 matches, groups putting most of their damage on healers killed in 19% of phases against 13% on other players (healer focus did better, contradicting the general claim); Bounty's narrower point (time spent on a monk late in the match) isn't tested.

claims.claim: push's snare character was soloed by Team's warrior while the 8 was out with the split instead of defending; push lost a second knight.

check.evidence: push's Snare died at 4:16 in its own base (6v4); push lost knights at 2:10 and 4:29.

claims.claim: push's returns were slow for a monk spike; letting Team set up on both fronts is the worst case for this build.

check.evidence: Shadow Step speed and coverage could be measured from positions; not done.

claims.claim: On top of that, Team boosts.

check.evidence: Team boosted at 5:44.

claims.claim: push collapsed before its snare character could snare, which wastes the collapse.

check.evidence: Across 144 matches a collapse with a snare carrier killed a splitter 20% of the time against 11% without (supported; the order of arrival, snare first, isn't measured).

claims.claim: A monk spike defends splits with the 6 and the 8 in its base; push's 8 kept following the main team and was soloed.

check.evidence: push lost its pit piece by piece: archers 4:45 and 7:29, Bodyguard 8:52.

claims.claim: push copied a meta bar and changed it: the 6 has only one real snare (Siphon Speed), which one Blight removes.

check.evidence: The engine's skill data counts three snare skills on push's Snare (Siphon Speed, Caltrops, Return); Return is mainly an escape, so 'one real snare' is close to Bounty's reading.

claims.claim: At 14 minutes push had put no real death penalty on Team, had no pit NPCs left, and only its position kept it in the game.

check.evidence: push had lost both knights, two archers and the Bodyguard by 8:52; Team had 5 deaths by 14:00, not none.

claims.claim: Behind at 20 minutes, a team should keep fighting for every edge (spikes, death penalty) until about 26:00, then take a gamble to finish.

check.evidence: A plan; the late-game choice could be priced in step 4.

6f7743eb-940d-5cc3-aa5b-32c17a66bf5a.alignment: Book wipe 1:21 to 3:06, Book Assassin death after time 2:03, Book Mes/A death 3:43, 옷옷옷옷's three-player split 3:45, Book split 4:53, Book wipe 4:55 to 5:41

claims.claim: Against a pressure build, expect the pressure team to kill slowly and the spike team to kill one target fast.

check.evidence: 옷옷옷옷's spikes killed Book's Prot, AoB Derv and Assassin from 1:36; Book's pressure killed no one.

claims.claim: Book had all the tools for catching spikes (Reversal of Fortune on the 8, Life Sheath and Spirit Bond on the 6, Infuse on the 7).

check.evidence: Book still lost six players by 3:43.

claims.claim: Book lost its assassin after time on his shield set, which is costly.

check.evidence: Book's Assassin died at 2:03 (after time).

claims.claim: Book always had someone timed or stuck, so it never had a moment to play tactics and was simply overwhelmed.

check.evidence: Book had 13 deaths by 5:37.

claims.claim: Book split with three including its 8 monk, leaving two monks at main; the answer (one damage, the smite) was enough.

check.evidence: Book's split (4:53: AoB Derv, 8 Monk, Mes/A) lost its Paragon at 4:55 and achieved nothing.

claims.claim: Book should have started splitting earlier, though it never had a free moment.

check.evidence: A choice not taken.
